TPI_PROCEDURE_01/15/2026.procedureDescription: The patient was placed in a comfortable prone/seated position. The target trigger points in the indicated musculature were palpated and marked. The overlying skin was prepped in standard sterile fashion using ChloraPrep. A 25-gauge, 1.5-inch needle was inserted directly into the taut bands of the trigger points. Negative aspiration for blood or bodily fluids was confirmed in multiple planes. A total of 4 mL of 1% preservative-free Lidocaine was injected into the identified trigger points. Local twitch responses were elicited followed by notable relaxation of the muscle band. The needle was withdrawn, and direct hemostatic pressure was applied. Sterile bandages were placed over the injection sites. The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate adverse events or complications.

TECAR_PROCEDURE_01/20/2026.anatomicalRegion: Neck / Cervical Spine, Mid Back / Thoracic, Wrist, Headaches / Concussion
TECAR_PROCEDURE_01/20/2026.clinicalNotes: Patient received targeted TECAR therapy to Neck / Cervical Spine, Mid Back / Thoracic, Wrist, Headaches / Concussion. Capacitive (CET) mode applied for superficial vascularization and deep resistive (RET) mode applied for deep fascial relaxation. Patient tolerated procedure well with immediate decrease in palpable muscle spasm and improved local tissue pliability.

FM_COUNSELING_FORM_6.session3Text: Session focused on processing acute trauma triggers associated with the CLINICAL_VISIT. Utilized cognitive restructuring to address intrusive thoughts and vehicular hyperarousal. Patient was instructed in somatic grounding and 4-7-8 diaphragmatic breathing to manage sudden distress in transit settings. Patient demonstrated good comprehension and receptivity.
FM_COUNSELING_FORM_6.session4Text: Addressed persistent catastrophic beliefs and driving-related apprehension. Explored avoidance behaviors interfering with daily functional transit. Introduced graduated behavioral exposure strategies and cognitive reframing techniques to reduce anticipatory anxiety. Patient engaged actively in identifying cognitive distortions.
FM_COUNSELING_FORM_6.session5Text: Explored the reciprocal relationship between ongoing physical musculoskeletal pain (cervical and lumbar strain) and elevated psychological distress/frustration. Introduced Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) adapted to avoid physical strain. Patient reported mild tension reduction post-exercise and committed to home practice.
FM_COUNSELING_FORM_6.session6Text: Session targeted sleep disturbance, nighttime trauma hyperarousal, and vehicular transit anxiety. Implemented stimulus control and sleep hygiene principles to address post-accident insomnia and nightmares. Discussed active coping strategies for unexpected passenger distress. Patient exhibited improved insight into emotional triggers.
FM_COUNSELING_FORM_6.session7Text: Reviewed and consolidated cognitive coping mechanisms utilized during recent vehicular transit. Patient reported decreased frequency and intensity of acute anxiety spikes when traveling as a passenger. Continued reinforcement of grounding tools and positive self-talk. Patient demonstrated improved emotional regulation.
FM_COUNSELING_FORM_6.session8Text: Comprehensive review of therapeutic progress and functional gains since initial assessment. Evaluated progress toward treatment plan goals, noting significant reduction in vehicular avoidance. Established a comprehensive relapse prevention plan and self-directed coping regimen for long-term emotional resilience.

DAVS_PROG.subjective: Patient presents for clinical progress evaluation following motor vehicle accident. Reports moderate interval reduction in acute cervical and lumbar paraspinal discomfort following initial sessions of Extracorporeal Shockwave Therapy (ESWT). Current pain rated 5-6/10 (improved from initial 8/10). Primary complaints remain muscular stiffness, localized soreness with prolonged sitting or driving, and end-of-day fatigue.
DAVS_PROG.objective: Palpation reveals discrete hyperirritable myofascial taut bands and active trigger points over the bilateral cervical, upper trapezius, and lumbar paraspinal musculature. Range of motion (ROM) displays moderate restriction (15-20%) secondary to muscular guarding and discomfort at terminal limits. Upper and lower extremity neurological examination remains non-focal. Reflexes 2+ bilaterally.
DAVS_PROG.plan:
1. Continue Extracorporeal Shockwave Therapy (ESWT Radial protocol: 2.0-2.5 bar, 15 Hz, 2,000-2,500 pulses) twice weekly targeting hyperirritable myofascial trigger zones.
2. Initiate gentle active-assisted stretching and therapeutic exercise for cervical/lumbar mobility.
3. Postural re-education for seated and driving mechanics.
4. Clinical re-evaluation of functional progress in 2 weeks.

DAVS_PROG_PAGE_2.subjective: Patient presents for follow-up progress evaluation. Reports clinically significant improvement in cervical and lumbar spinal symptoms following course of Extracorporeal Shockwave Therapy (ESWT). Current pain rated 2-3/10 on average. Patient notes substantial gains in functional capacity, sitting tolerance, and driving duration without severe exacerbation. Occasional mild tightness after strenuous activity which resolves with stretching.
DAVS_PROG_PAGE_2.objective: Physical re-examination demonstrates marked reduction in paraspinal muscle hypertonicity and trigger point sensitivity across cervical and lumbar regions. Significantly enhanced soft tissue compliance. Active range of motion (ROM) in cervical and lumbar spine is within 90-95% of expected baseline with minimal end-range discomfort. Motor strength 5/5 bilaterally, deep tendon reflexes symmetrical (2+), no sensory deficits.
DAVS_PROG_PAGE_2.plan:
1. Transition from intensive shockwave protocol to maintenance ESWT therapy.
2. Progress dynamic core strengthening, postural stabilization, and independent home exercise program.
3. Educate on ergonomic body mechanics and flare-up management.
4. Comprehensive final outcome evaluation and discharge assessment scheduled in 2-3 weeks.
